questions.question: For the paper's one-element, closed-system model, what quantity is proposed as inversely related to organization?

options.A: The sum of the action integrals of the system's elements
options.B: The total kinetic energy at one instant
options.D: The duration of motion regardless of trajectory

questions.rationale: The authors define organization as reciprocal to the sum of actions and specialize to one element.
questions.evidence_quote: Here we show that the amount of organization is inversely proportional

questions.question: Why can the potential energy be set to zero in the model's assumptions?

options.A: The element is force-free, so potential energy is constant and its arbitrary zero can be chosen
options.B: The system is open and radiates all potential energy
options.C: The constraint performs work that exactly cancels potential energy
options.D: The model assumes the kinetic energy is zero

questions.rationale: Assumption 1 treats the particle as free and chooses the arbitrary potential-energy origin.
questions.evidence_quote: the potential energy is a constant and can be set to be zero

questions.question: What role does fixing the trajectory endpoints at opposite square corners play in the model?

options.A: It prevents the action integral from approaching zero because the endpoints cannot become arbitrarily close
options.B: It guarantees every possible trajectory has the same length
options.C: It ensures the action integral becomes infinite
options.D: It removes the need for a constraint

questions.rationale: The endpoint condition supplies a nonzero lower bound on trajectory length/action.
questions.evidence_quote: the end points cannot get inﬁnitely close together.

questions.question: Which additional assumption is used to convert the action integral's time interval into trajectory length?

options.A: An isotropic medium and constant speed, so Δt=l/v
options.B: A dissipative medium where v changes linearly
options.C: A circular orbit with constant angular momentum
options.D: A relativistic speed limit that fixes Δt

questions.rationale: The model invokes isotropy and constant speed to substitute path length for time.
questions.evidence_quote: The consequence of this assumption is that the constant velocity of the element allows us to substitute the interval of time with the length of the trajectory

questions.question: Given equal mass and speed, how does the derivation relate the action to trajectory length?

options.A: I=(C1/v)l, so action is proportional to path length
options.B: I=C1/l, so action falls as paths lengthen
options.C: I is independent of l because kinetic energy is constant
options.D: I is proportional to l² because the system is two-dimensional

questions.rationale: Equation (12) expresses action as constant kinetic energy times elapsed time and substitutes Δt=l/v.
questions.evidence_quote: where l is the length of the trajectory of the element in each case

questions.question: If state 1's least-action path is twice as long as state 2's, what organization ratio does the paper derive?

options.D: The ratio cannot be determined without the particle mass

questions.rationale: With the same constants, organization scales as inverse path length, so halving l doubles organization.

questions.question: Why does the paper exclude a completely blocked path when defining its model?

options.A: Such a constraint could make the trajectory infinitely long and the action infinite
options.B: It would make the particle's mass change
options.C: It would make the system open
options.D: It would force the action to be zero

questions.rationale: Assumption 5 rules out infinite trajectory length and thus infinite action.
questions.evidence_quote: the trajectory cannot become inﬁnitely long.

questions.question: What is the stated status of the constraint in the one-element illustration?

options.A: It changes the action by altering the allowed path but does not interact with the element
options.B: It exerts a friction force proportional to speed
options.C: It supplies the kinetic energy required for motion
options.D: It is treated as a second dynamical element

questions.rationale: The setup treats the constraint geometrically and assumes no interaction with the particle.
questions.evidence_quote: The element does not interact with the constraint.

questions.question: What specific numerical example is used to illustrate the comparison between two configurations?

options.A: If l1=2l2, state 2 is said to be twice as organized as state 1
options.B: If l1=2l2, state 1 is said to be twice as organized as state 2
options.C: If l1=l2, state 2 is 50% more organized
options.D: If l1=4l2, the two states have equal organization

questions.rationale: The paper applies its inverse-length result to the case where the first path is twice as long.

questions.question: What limitation does the authors' discussion explicitly assign to this installment of the model?

options.A: It treats only a closed, nondissipative system with one free particle and one constraint
options.B: It already applies to arbitrary open systems with many interacting particles
options.C: It requires a dissipative many-body system
options.D: It is limited to systems where the constraint interacts with each element

questions.rationale: The discussion restricts the present paper to a simple case and postpones broader extensions.
questions.evidence_quote: limited only to closed, nondissipative system with one free particle as an element, and one constraint.
